messages:
security-oncall: SBOM scanner flagged a HIGH CVE in a transitive npm dep inside redwood/api-worker:prod-2026-03-18. snippet attached. :eyes:
build-bot: automated-scan -> vuln: CVE-2025-3456 (high) via fastpipe@1.2.3 -> old-crypto@0.9.0; images: redwood/api-worker:prod-2026-03-18, redwood/ingest:prod-2026-03-17, redwood/etl:staging-2026-03-18
sara_eng: Are any of these actively exploited or showing anomalous traffic?
security-oncall: No signs of exploitation in logs so far. Detected during nightly SBOM sweep. Affects prod images in two clusters and staging. Recommend isolate build SA, rotate KMS signing key, and queue rebuilds.
jordan_sre: Rotate KMS how without breaking signature verification for existing images in the registry?
matt_sec: Proposed plan: 1) Create new key version in KMS. 2) Update signing pipeline to sign with new key v2. 3) Keep verification path tolerant to old key for 48h (fallback verification). 4) Quarantine affected images and trigger rebuilds, re-sign with v2. 5) Tighten RBAC for build service account.
nina_pm: Do we need to notify customers? Any data plane impact?
security-oncall: No customer-facing impact expected. Images will be rebuilt and re-signed; rollout will be gradual. I'll prepare comms if we find exploit artifacts.
sara_eng: Also observed: build service account (build-sa) has cloudkms.admin role. That's broader than needed. Propose sign-only role + explicit create-key permission removed.
jordan_sre: I'll draft an IAM change. Example (gcloud):
```
# remove admin
gcloud projects remove-iam-policy-binding redwood-prod \
  --member=serviceAccount:build-sa@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com \
  --role=roles/cloudkms.admin
# grant sign only
gcloud projects add-iam-policy-binding redwood-prod \
  --member=serviceAccount:build-sa@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com \
  --role=roles/cloudkms.signerVerifier
```
matt_sec: Add audit logging changes: enable KMS key access logs and export to secure audit bucket (encrypted, restricted). Retain 90d, alert on key.create, key.version.create, and unusual signer activity.
security-oncall: +1. I'll open the emergency PR to fail builds at SBOM gate on any transitive HIGH severities (with a 24h allowlist override for triage).
sara_eng: Short-term: can we patch the transitive dep instead of full rebuild? Maybe a vendored patch or webpack shim?
matt_sec: We can attempt a code-level shim to mitigate old-crypto usage in the short term, but we still need CI rebuilds to get new image signatures. Longer fix is updating the dependency tree or contributing the patch upstream.
jordan_sre: I'm revoking deploy tokens for build-sa now to stop any new images signing with old key. Will rotate in 10m and post status.
build-bot: token_revoke: build-sa deploy token revoked @1893214660
jordan_sre: rotation complete. New key version created: projects/redwood/locations/global/keyRings/prod/cryptoKeys/img-sign v2. URL: (internal link)
sara_eng: Kicked off CI rebuilds for affected images. small queue; ETA ~45m for first pass.
nina_pm: I'll draft an internal incident note and postmortem skeleton. No external comms unless signs of exploitation.
security-oncall: No exploitation found. Postmortem to include: SBOM freshness gap, RBAC gap for build-sa, missing key-access alerts, and insufficient SBOM gating. Assigning actions.
matt_sec: I'll create tickets: ENG-Restrict-Build-SA-RBAC, INFRA-Enable-KMS-Logging, DEVEX-SBOM-Docs, SEC-Audit-Run.
jordan_sre: CI rebuilds passing, images re-signed with v2, rolling deploys in progress. Will close incident after 4h of stable telemetry.
security-oncall: :white_check_mark: Thanks everyone. I'll follow up with the postmortem draft and action owners.
